text: When checkout latency triples in production, someone has to find out why, prove it, and fix it — usually under time pressure, jumping between a dashboard, a deploy log, and a terminal. Sentinel agent does the investigation and the proof. It does not do the fix without a human.

Here is the incident it's been handed. Checkout latency has risen sharply, and the agent is told to investigate, compute the real magnitude, and only prepare a fix if the evidence actually supports one.

It starts reaching real systems immediately. These are genuine calls against a real tool server — not simulated in the frontend. It pulls the incident, the deployment history, and the diff of the most recent change.

Three sub agents are dispatched in parallel, each investigating a different angle — performance, deployment timing, and the code itself. Each runs in its own context, and only its conclusion comes back to the root agent.
This is the sandbox. The agent writes its own Python to compute the actual regression from raw metrics — not a number it read off a table, a number it calculated itself.

And here is the moment the entire product exists for. It has finished investigating, and it has a fix ready — but it stops here. It shows the exact tool call, the exact arguments, and the mechanism it found, and it waits for a human.
The evidence is a real mechanism, not a guess based on timing, so I'm approving it. Declining was just as available — the agent would have simply stopped.

The rollback runs, and the agent checks its own work — service health flips back to healthy. And this line, on the right, is not the agent's report. It's the estate's own independent log of what actually changed.
Real tools. A real sandbox. Real delegation. And a real approval gate that held until a human clicked it. Built on TrueForge.
